title: kit.upload-policy.v1
description: What one form accepts as a file (@saasreport/uploads): the file fields it declares, the types it allows (decided from the file's own bytes, never from its name or declared type), the size caps, retention, and what happens to a file the pipeline cannot clear. A form without a policy takes no files and rejects file parts. Nothing is hardcoded in a handler: the policy is data, validated here.

id.description: Stable id, copied into every UploadRecord (policy_id) so a verdict can be traced to the rule that produced it.

file_fields.description: The multipart field names that may carry a file. A file part under any other name is rejected (file_field_not_accepted).

allowed_types.description: Sniffed types the form accepts (the sniffer's list, see ALLOWABLE_TYPES in @saasreport/uploads). Executables, scripts and archives other than OOXML are never allowable.

max_bytes.description: Largest single file. 64 MiB at most: the Worker holds the bytes to hash and triage them (128 MiB isolate); larger files take a presigned direct upload into quarantine.

max_request_bytes.description: Largest whole multipart request. Defaults to max_bytes times the total file count plus 1 MiB of fields.

max_field_bytes.description: Largest text field of the form (default 65536).

retention_days.description: A released upload is deleted this many days after receipt (tombstone kept).

blocked_retention_days.description: A held or blocked object is deleted from quarantine after this many days unless on hold.

on_needs_sandbox.description: What the form does with a file whose verdict is needs_sandbox (which is what a project with no scanner configured gets for every file): hold it in quarantine until a person decides, or release it for download only. The verdict stays needs_sandbox either way; there is no implicit pass.

scanner.description: Name of the scanner the project wired for this form (createUploads({ scanners })). Absent: none, and every file is needs_sandbox.

origin.description: The cookieless origin released files are served from.

inline_types.description: The kinds this form declares inline-safe: a released upload of exactly one of these sniffed types is served without Content-Disposition: attachment, under the restrictive image CSP (kit.upload-serve.v1). Raster images only: SVG, HTML, XML, script, PDF and Office files are never inline, whatever this says. Absent or empty: every download is an attachment.

limits.description: Triage limits, each within the hard ceiling of the engine (TRIAGE_CEILING). Omitted ones take TRIAGE_DEFAULTS.
